source: ICAI CA Intermediate Paper 4 MCQ booklets with answer keys (icai.org, 'MCQ Questions and Keys')
note: Only for the trap reel. Answers are ICAI's official keys; 'trap' is our reading of the tempting wrong option.

questions.chapter_title: P/V ratio after a price cut
questions.text: PS Limited plans to reduce its selling price by 5%. Variable cost is 76% of the current selling price. Find the P/V ratio after reducing the price by 5%. (a) 20% (b) 24% (c) 25.26% (d) 19%
questions.trap_why: ₹19 is the new contribution on a ₹100 price, but the new price is ₹95, so P/V = 19 ÷ 95 = 20%

questions.text: Production overheads are absorbed at ₹20 per machine hour. Actual overheads were ₹12,00,000, including ₹80,000 obsolete stores written off and ₹30,000 strike-period wages under an award. Actual machine hours were 50,000. Production was 20,000 units and sales 18,000 units. What under-absorbed overhead is charged to cost of sales? (a) ₹91,000 (b) ₹90,000 (c) ₹81,000 (d) ₹80,000
questions.trap_why: ₹90,000 is the whole under-absorption (10,90,000 − 10,00,000), but only the sold part goes to cost of sales: 90,000 × 18,000 ÷ 20,000 = 81,000

questions.text: Exercise bikes to be sold: January 1,500, February 1,800. Closing stock of finished bikes is kept at 20% of next month's sales. Each bike needs one main body and two pedals. How many pedals must be purchased for January production? (a) 1,560 pedals (b) 1,640 pedals (c) 3,120 pedals (d) 2,880 pedals
questions.trap_why: 1,560 is the number of bikes (1,500 + 360 − 300); each bike needs two pedals, so 3,120

questions.text: Opening stock of Material A: 100 units at ₹50. Purchases: 2,500 units at ₹55 on 5 Oct and 600 units at ₹56 on 8 Oct. Issue: 1,500 units on 15 Oct. What is the value of material consumed under LIFO? (a) ₹83,100 (b) ₹82,000 (c) ₹82,500 (d) ₹84,000
questions.trap_why: ₹82,000 is FIFO (100 at ₹50 + 1,400 at ₹55); LIFO takes the latest first: 600 × 56 + 900 × 55 = 83,100

questions.text: Process-I: input 10,000 units; materials ₹1,60,000, wages ₹70,000, overheads ₹58,000. Normal loss is 6% of input; scrap sells at ₹10 a unit. Output of 9,200 units goes to Process-II. What is the value of units transferred? (a) ₹2,76,000 (b) ₹2,82,000 (c) ₹2,88,000 (d) ₹2,78,000
questions.trap_why: ₹2,82,000 passes on the whole net cost, but 200 units were lost abnormally: (2,88,000 − 6,000) ÷ 9,400 normal units = ₹30, × 9,200 = 2,76,000

questions.text: Maximum stock level 1,125 units, re-order level 750 units, minimum consumption 25 units a day, minimum lead time 5 days. What is the re-order quantity? (a) 375 units (b) 450 units (c) 500 units (d) 600 units
questions.trap_why: 1,125 − 750 forgets the stock used up during the lead time; Max = ROL + ROQ − min usage × min lead time, so ROQ = 1,125 − 750 + 125 = 500

questions.text: Budget: 40,000 units with fixed overheads ₹78,000. Actual: 48,000 units with fixed overheads ₹84,000. Calculate the fixed overhead volume variance. (a) ₹15,600 F (b) ₹15,600 A (c) ₹6,000 A (d) ₹14,000 A
questions.trap_why: producing more than budget recovers more fixed overhead, so the volume variance is favourable: (48,000 − 40,000) × ₹1.95 = 15,600 F

questions.text: Standard time is 30 minutes a unit at ₹50 an hour. 30,000 units were made; the labour rate variance was ₹7,500 adverse and the efficiency variance was nil. What was the actual wage cost per unit? (a) ₹50.00 (b) ₹25.50 (c) ₹50.50 (d) ₹25.25
questions.trap_why: ₹50.50 is the actual rate per hour (7,500 ÷ 15,000 hours = 50 paise extra); per unit it is half an hour: ₹25.25

questions.text: Opening raw material stock ₹25,000, closing stock ₹75,000, raw material consumed ₹7,50,000. For how many days is average inventory held? (360 days a year) (a) 14 days (b) 15 days (c) 24 days (d) 26 days
questions.trap_why: 15 is the turnover ratio (7,50,000 ÷ 50,000), not days; days = 360 ÷ 15 = 24

questions.text: On 1 April 150 workers were employed. During the year 30 resigned and 5 were discharged; 15 were replaced. What is the labour turnover rate by the separation method? (a) 21.43% (b) 18% (c) 25% (d) 30%
questions.trap_why: 21.43% counts only the 30 resignations; separations include discharges: 35 ÷ average 140 = 25%

questions.text: Spare parts cost last month: Machine A ₹40,000, Machine B ₹60,000. Next month spare part prices rise 15% for both machines, and consumption rises 25% for Machine B only. What is next month's total spare parts cost? (a) ₹1,25,000 (b) ₹1,43,750 (c) ₹1,26,500 (d) ₹1,32,250
questions.trap_why: ₹1,43,750 applies the 25% to both machines; only B uses more: 40,000 × 1.15 + 60,000 × 1.25 × 1.15 = 1,32,250

questions.text: A lorry leaves X with 15 tonnes, unloads 5 tonnes at Y and the rest at Z, and returns from Z to X with 8 tonnes. X–Y 50 km, Y–Z 60 km, Z–X 80 km. Find absolute and commercial tonne-km. (a) 1,690 & 2,000 (b) 1,990 & 2,090 (c) 2,090 & 1,990 (d) 2,100 & 1,980
questions.trap_why: the two are swapped: absolute adds each leg (750 + 600 + 640 = 1,990), commercial is average load 11 × 190 km = 2,090

questions.text: Joint products X (200 units at ₹350) and Y (400 units at ₹250) use material ₹80,000 and labour ₹40,000; fixed overheads are ₹20,000. Under the contribution margin method, in what ratio are fixed overheads apportioned between X and Y? (a) 4 : 8 (b) 3 : 2 (c) 2 : 3 (d) 8 : 4
questions.trap_why: 4 : 8 is just the units; the method uses contribution: X 200 × (350 − 200) = 30,000, Y 400 × (250 − 200) = 20,000, so 3 : 2

questions.text: Annual need for raw material OE is 1,600 kg at ₹200 a kg. Ordering cost is ₹500 an order; storage costs ₹2.5 a kg a month; interest is 1.25% a quarter. What is the EOQ? (a) 200 kgs (b) 500 kgs (c) 400 kgs (d) 231 kgs
questions.trap_why: 231 counts only storage (₹30 a year); carrying cost also has interest, 5% of ₹200 = ₹10, so √(2 × 1,600 × 500 ÷ 40) = 200
